questions.question: What were the effects and required actions when wire feed motor overload alarms occurred on the WM-101 during the night shift?
questions.reference_answer: The WM-101 generated wire feed motor overload alarms three times on the night shift of 13 November 2024, at 23:14, 01:47, and 04:22. Each alarm stopped production for an average of 18 minutes while the operator cleared the fault and adjusted the wire tension, resulting in a total downtime of 54 minutes for the shift. During the third alarm at 04:22, the wire bird‑nested at the drive rolls, prompting the shift supervisor to be called to clear the nest and re‑thread the wire, which extended the downtime for that event to 35 minutes.

NON-CONFORMANCE REPORT
Equipment: WM-101 MIG Welder
Document Type: NCR
Reference: NCR-2024-047
Revision: 1.0
Plant: Greenfield Steel Works
Line: Fabrication Line 1
Raised by: Shift Supervisor — D. Kowalski
Date raised: 14 November 2024
Status: Closed

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. NON-CONFORMANCE DESCRIPTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WM-101 generated wire feed motor overload alarms on three separate
occasions during the night shift on 13 November 2024. The alarms
occurred at 23:14, 01:47, and 04:22.

Each alarm caused a production stop averaging 18 minutes while the
operator cleared the fault and adjusted wire tension. Total downtime
attributable to this fault: 54 minutes across the shift.

On the third alarm at 04:22, the wire birdnested at the drive rolls,
requiring the shift supervisor to be called to clear the nest and
re-thread the wire. This extended the downtime to 35 minutes for
the third event.
questions.review_notes: Trivia about one past night shift (alarm times, downtime minutes).

questions.question: What result got the quality inspection on parts welded at 01:47?
questions.reference_answer: The quality inspection, done by technician R. Singh on 14 November 2024, found 3 of the 12 parts welded during the 01:47 event had incomplete fusion at the weld root and were scrapped (Batch Reference: GS-NOV-0447). The remaining 41 parts passed visual inspection and were released.
source_text:
Parts welded during the 01:47 event were flagged for quality inspection
as arc instability was observed following the wire feed fault. Inspection
found 3 of 12 parts with incomplete fusion at the weld root. These parts
were scrapped (Batch Reference: GS-NOV-0447).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Following the third alarm, WM-101 was taken out of service for the
remainder of the shift. Production was transferred to WM-102 on
Fabrication Line 2 for the balance of the night shift.

All parts welded on WM-101 during the shift were quarantined pending
quality inspection. Inspection completed 14 November 2024 by quality
technician R. Singh.

Inspection result: 3 parts scrapped (incomplete root fusion). 
Remaining 41 parts passed visual inspection and were released.

3. ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintenance technician T. Baxter inspected WM-101 on 14 November 2024.

Findings:

3.1 Drive Rolls
Drive rolls showed significant groove wear. The 0.8mm groove had worn
to approximately 1.1mm measured width. This increased groove allows the
wire to sit lower in the groove, reducing grip and causing inconsistent
feed speed. When the operator increased tension to compensate, the
additional pressure caused motor overload.
questions.review_notes: Garbled question and the reference answer does not answer it.

questions.question: What is the recommended service interval for the drive rolls, and did the actual usage exceed this interval at the time of the incident?
questions.reference_answer: The recommended service interval for the drive rolls is 6 months or 500 production hours, whichever comes first. At the time of the incident, the drive rolls had accumulated 627 production hours, exceeding the 500‑hour limit and the 6‑month interval, indicating that the service interval had been surpassed.
source_text:
The drive rolls had not been replaced since the last recorded service
in March 2024 — 8 months of continuous production. Recommended service
interval is 6 months or 500 production hours, whichever comes first.
Service records showed 627 production hours on the current drive rolls
at the time of the incident.

3.2 Wire Liner
Liner inspection found the liner partially blocked at the point where
the torch neck bends. Wire debris had accumulated at the bend, increasing
resistance. This contributed to the motor overload condition in combination
with the worn drive rolls.

3.3 Root Cause — Primary
Worn drive rolls beyond service interval. Drive rolls should have been
replaced at the 6-month / 500-hour service in September 2024.
Service was not completed due to line demand during the autumn production
peak. The service was deferred without a rescheduled date being set.
questions.review_notes: Real spec: drive roll interval 6 months / 500 hours, and it was exceeded (627 h).

questions.question: What are the part numbers for the WM-101 drive rolls, wire liner and contact tip?
questions.reference_answer: Drive rolls GSW-DROLL-08, wire liner GSW-LINER-08, contact tip GSW-TIP-08 (the 0.8 mm parts fitted in the NCR-2024-047 corrective action).
source_text:
3.4 Root Cause — Contributing
Wire liner partially blocked, increasing feed resistance. Liner should
have been inspected as part of the deferred September service.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4.1 Immediate corrective action (completed 14 November 2024)
  - Drive rolls replaced: Part No. GSW-DROLL-08, fitted by T. Baxter
  - Wire liner replaced: Part No. GSW-LINER-08, fitted by T. Baxter
  - Contact tip replaced as precaution: Part No. GSW-TIP-08
  - Burn-in procedure completed per WI-WM101-001
  - Test welds ran and inspected — all passed
  - WM-101 returned to service 14 November 2024 at 14:30
questions.review_notes: Rewritten from incident history into the part numbers it contains.
questions.original_question: What burn-in procedure was performed on the WM-101 during the November 2024 corrective action?
questions.original_reference_answer: The burn-in procedure was completed per WI-WM101-001 as part of the immediate corrective action on 14 November 2024. It followed the replacement of drive rolls (Part No. GSW-DROLL-08), wire liner (Part No. GSW-LINER-08), and contact tip (Part No. GSW-TIP-08), after which test welds were run and inspected, all passing, and the WM-101 was returned to service at 14:30.

questions.question: When I keep gettin three or more wire fead motor overlad alrms in a single shift, what steps shoud I take as a maintenence tech to address the issue and avoid further problems?
questions.reference_answer: The occurrence of three or more wire feed motor overload alarms in a single shift is a reliable indicator of worn drive rolls or a blocked liner, not an operator error. The correct response is to stop production immediately and conduct a full inspection of the drive rolls and liner rather than continuing to adjust tension. Operators should escalate the problem to maintenance right away. Continuing production despite repeated overload alarms can lead to motor burnout, weld quality defects from inconsistent wire feed speed, arc instability events that cause parts to be scrapped, and birdnesting events that result in extended downtime.

When wire feed motor overload alarms occur three or more times in a
single shift, this is a reliable indicator of worn drive rolls or a
blocked liner — not an operator error. The correct response is to
stop production and conduct a full drive roll and liner inspection
rather than continuing to adjust tension.

Continuing production with repeated overload alarms risks:
  - Motor burnout (expensive repair, long lead time for replacement)
  - Weld quality defects from inconsistent wire feed speed
  - Arc instability events causing parts to be scrapped
  - Birdnesting events causing extended downtime

Operators who encounter three or more wire feed overload alarms in a
shift should escalate to maintenance immediately rather than attempting
further tension adjustments.
questions.review_notes: Misspelled on purpose (robustness); answer is the key safety rule: stop, inspect, don't keep adjusting tension.

This SOP defines the correct operating procedure for the WM-101 MIG Welder

questions.question: How should the wire feed tension be set on the WM-101, and what happens if it is too tight or too loose?
questions.reference_answer: Set wire feed tension finger-tight plus one quarter turn on the pressure arm. Too tight causes motor overload alarms; too loose causes wire slip and arc instability.
source_text:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRE-OPERATION CHECKS (complete before every shift)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2.1 Wire Feed System
- Inspect wire spool for kinks, birdnesting, or debris
- Confirm wire diameter matches job specification (standard: 0.8mm or 1.0mm)
- Check drive roll groove matches wire diameter — mismatched rolls cause overload
- Set wire feed tension: finger-tight plus one quarter turn on the pressure arm
- Too tight: motor overload alarms. Too loose: wire slip and arc instability.
- Pull wire through liner manually — resistance should be smooth with no snags
- If resistance is uneven or wire snags, inspect liner for kinks or replace
questions.review_notes: Six questions in one; cut down to the tension question, answer taken word-for-word from SOP 2.1.
questions.original_question: Hey i need to know what i gotta do with the wire spool before i start the shift like how i check it for kinks or birdnesting what diameter i should be looking for how i match the drive roll groove how i set the tension and what happens if its too tight or too loose and also what i do if i feel resistance pulling the wire through the liner
questions.original_reference_answer: Before each shift you must inspect the wire spool for kinks, bird‑nesting, or debris. Confirm that the wire diameter matches the job specification – the standard sizes are 0.8 mm or 1.0 mm. Check that the drive‑roll groove matches the wire diameter; a mismatch will cause overload. Set the wire‑feed tension to finger‑tight plus a quarter turn on the pressure arm. If the tension is too tight the machine will give motor‑overload alarms; if it is too loose the wire will slip and the arc will become unstable. Pull the wire through the liner by hand; the pull should be smooth with no snags. If the resistance is uneven or you feel snags, inspect the liner for kinks or replace it.
